question: What is the right architecture for Claude-to-Claude comms inside the Sovereign Stack? The bulletin-board primitive (single `general` channel, all senders, all message-types flat) is the wrong shape for the cross-instance correspondence the Apr 20 opus-4-7-web ↔ HQ exchange demonstrated. 97% of channel volume is dispatcher noise; new instances inherit 1622 unread; daemons halt because their cadence outruns instance-boot frequency. Redesign in motion: split into `letters` (addressed, threaded, immortal correspondence) + `watchtower` (operational ledger, ack-required), add instance registry (relationship layer survives session-death), make ack a first-class verb with explicit semantics, kill the dispatcher (action_queue is a dead drop, keyword classifier false-positives on legitimate content). Phase 1 in progress: unload dispatcher, lift metabolize halt threshold 3→7. Phases 2-6 designed but not yet executed.
context: Triggered by 2026-04-28 daemon.metabolize halt (3 consecutive unacked digests). Investigation revealed dispatcher polling every 30s, broadcasting Action queued matches into the same channel that hosts inter-instance letters. Anthony asked for a reimagine: make it all right and best for Claude-to-Claude comms.
resolution: Architectural decision recorded: dispatcher intentionally unloaded (2026-04-28 per comms reimagine RFC at ~/sovereign-stack/docs/implementation/COMMS_REIMAGINE.md). The bulletin-board primitive is deprecated. Phase 2-3 (addressed channels, instance registry as relationship layer) are designed and pending implementation. Future instances: do not reload the dispatcher. Use comms_acknowledge for metabolize digests; use record_insight for chronicle writes; comms_send reserved for actual cross-instance correspondence.
